tier_reason: Author's own blog post with tok/s tables vs llama.cpp and a GFLOPS figure vs MKL on named CPUs; kernels are public but compiler version/flags for the reported runs and a runnable benchmark harness are not fully stated, so not A; first-party, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 'prompt eval time with llamafile should go anywhere between 30% and 500% faster when using F16 and Q8_0 weights on CPU'; Mistral 7B f16 on Threadripper 7995WX: llamafile-0.7 485 vs llama.cpp 2024-03-29 197 prompt tok/s (eval 17 vs 16); TinyLlama f16 on Raspberry Pi 5: 62 vs 28 prompt tok/s (eval 5 vs 5); 810 GFLOPS on i9-14900K for a 513x512 * 512x512 matmul vs MKL 295 GFLOPS at that size
corrections.hardware: AMD Threadripper 7995WX; Raspberry Pi 5; Intel i9-14900K (plus others on the page)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: -O3 -ffast-math -march=native mentioned for the example kernel; flags for the tok/s runs not stated
corrections.caveats: Author's own blog post; PR https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/6414 reports ~40% on Q4_0/Q8_0 and 2x on F16 with user reports. Gains are on prompt eval (prefill) only; token generation is roughly unchanged (memory-bound). Baseline is the March-2024 llama.cpp, which has since merged these kernels. MKL comparison is a single matrix size.

notes: Record said 790 GFLOPS; page says 810 GFLOPS on i9-14900K. Metadata confirmed: Apache-2.0, 26.1k stars, last commit 2026-09-30, not archived.

tier_reason: Upgraded: peer-reviewed MLSys 2020 paper benchmarks MNN against CoreML, TF-Lite, NCNN and MACE on named phones (A11, Snapdragon 835, Kirin 980) and reports ~20-40% wins; no compiler flags/benchmark-code link in the paper, so B not A.

corrections.baseline: TensorFlow Lite, NCNN, MACE, CoreML (MLSys 2020 paper)
corrections.claimed_speedup: MLSys 2020 paper: 'MNN outperforms other inference engines under almost all settings by about 20%~40%' (about 30% faster CPU inference on iOS, 34% on Android) on MobileNet-v1, SqueezeNet-v1.1, ResNet-18; README separately claims 'Twice speed increase' for ARM v8.2 FP16 and '2.5 faster to use sdot for ARM v8.2 and VNNI' (vs its own FP32/non-sdot paths)
corrections.hardware: iPhone 8 / iPhone X (Apple A11), Xiaomi MI6 (Snapdragon 835), Huawei Mate 20 (Kirin 980)
corrections.workload: Mobile CNN inference latency (MobileNet-v1, SqueezeNet-v1.1, ResNet-18, 224x224) on phone CPUs and GPUs (OpenCL/Vulkan/OpenGL/Metal).
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed but authored by the MNN team (Alibaba); results from 2020-era phones and engine versions. No XNNPACK/oneDNN comparison. README FP16/sdot speedups are vs MNN's own other paths, not vs a competitor.

notes: Tier raised C->B on the MLSys 2020 paper (read via ar5iv). Metadata confirmed: Apache-2.0, 16.0k stars, last commit 2026-09-30.

tier_reason: First-party README tables with benchmark binary (ni_bench_cuda) and RTX 4090 / M4 Pro hardware, but no compiler versions/flags beyond CMake Release; the README itself shows it is slower than cuBLAS's proper TN path at every size and slower than or equal to ONNX Runtime on all three CPU models.

corrections.hardware: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89) for GPU; Apple M4 Pro for CPU
corrections.claimed_speedup: int8 GEMM vs cuBLAS called with row-major B (NN): 2.09x at n=256, 1.26x at 512, 1.24x at 1024, 0.73x at 2048, 0.71x at 4096; vs cuBLAS TN, cuBLAS is 1.6x-4.5x faster at every size. CPU engine vs ONNX Runtime: MNIST 49 vs 48 us (0.99x), Keyword Spotting 110 vs 67 us (0.60x), Visual Wake Words 240 vs 184 us (0.77x)

notes: Author concedes the cuBLAS win is an artifact of calling cuBLAS in its slow NN layout; CPU engine is 1.0-0.6x of ORT. If the orchestrator keeps flagged entries, record shortcoming: not faster than incumbent on its proper path.
